Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 L.A.A.S.No.375 of 2006
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada) This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is preferred by the Land Acquisition Officer, RDO,
Nizamabad, aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 16.08.2005 passed in O.P.No.461 of 1995 by the learned I Additional District Judge, Nizamabad (hereinafter referred to as 'the reference Court').
2.
For convenience and clarity, the parties herein are referred to as they were arrayed before the reference Court.

3. The facts of the case in brief are that the Government has acquired an extent of Ac.02-02 gts., of patta lands classified as Single Crop Wet lands (SCW), Double Crop Wet (DCW) lands and also dry lands in several survey numbers at Mutyampally, hamlet of Amrad village for the purpose of providing house sites to Weaker Sections of people.
A draft notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was issued on 01.03.1994 and 03.03.1994.

After conducting due enquiry, the Land Acquisition officer has passed an award granting compensation of Rs.20,000/- per acre for the land to an AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.375_2006 extent of Ac.0-25 guntas in survey Nos.696 and 699 (DCW and SCW)
and @Rs.12,100/- for the lands to an extent of Ac.01-17 guntas in survey Nos.700 and 702 (dry lands).
Aggrieved by the said award, the claimants have filed a petition for reference and the same was referred under Section 18 of the Act to the reference Court.

4. The reference Court has framed the following issues for consideration:
"1.
Whether
the claimants are entitled to enhancement of compensation and consequential benefits thereon under the amended LA Act and if so, at what rate?

2. To what relief?"
5.
Before the reference Court, the claimants got examined PWs 1 to 3 and got marked Exs.A1 to A3.
On behalf of the respondents, RW1 was examined and Ex.B1 was marked.

sentences.text:
Based on the evidence on record, the reference Court has enhanced the compensation to Rs.57,000/- per acre for the extent of Ac.0-25 guntas in survey Nos.696 and 699 and @ Rs.34,200/-
per acre for the extent of Ac.01-17 guntas in survey Nos.700 and 702, of the acquired lands apart from the other statutory benefits.
Aggrieved by the said enhancement, the Land Acquisition Officer has preferred the present appeal.
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.375_2006 7.

Heard the submissions of learned Government Pleader for the appellant and Sri V.Manohar Rao,
learned counsel for respondent Nos.2, 5, 6 and 7.
8.
Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the reference Court has erred in enhancing the compensation by relying on Ex.A1 without any other corroborative evidence.

He further argued that the lands under Exs.A1 to A3 are not similar for assessing the market value of the acquired lands and that the reference Court has enhanced the compensation without following any settled principles of assessment.
9. The learned respondents counsel, on the other hand, submitted that the reference Court has passed a well reasoned order and thus has prayed to dismiss the appeal.

10. Based on the above rival contentions, this Court frames the following points for determination:
1.
Whether the claimants are not entitled for enhancement of compensation?
2. Whether the judgment and decree of the reference Court need any interference?

3. To what relief?
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.375_2006 11. POINT NO.1:
a) PW1 is the claimant No.5.

His evidence reveals that their lands are fertile lands and that they used to cultivate turmeric, maize, chilies, vegetables, paddy and other commercial crops and that their village is just 4 KM away from Nizamabad and that the land under Ex.A1 is similar in nature, fertility and potentiality to that of acquired land.

b) A perusal of Ex.A1 sale deed reveals that, land to an extent of 16  guntas SCW in survey No.836 situated at Amrad village was sold for a value of Rs.22,000/- i.e. @
Rs.53,333/- per acre.
c) PW3 is a resident of Manik Bhandar village and he is also one of the claimants.

It is elicited through him during his cross examination that their village Manik Bhandar is The Land Acquisition Officer Rdo, vs G. Ashanna on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125044796/
2 abutting to NH-16 and Mutyampalli village and that Mutyampalli village is a hamlet of Amrad village.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is elicited that the sale deed under Ex.A1 can be considered since it pertains to Amrad village and the land acquired happens to be in the hamlet (Mutyampally) of Amrad Village.

d) PW2 is claimant No.2, his evidence runs in similar lines to that of PW1 and further he relied upon Ex.A2, which is a copy of AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.375_2006 judgment and decree in O.P.No.174 of 1988 dated 31.03.1992 passed by the I Additional District Judge, Nizamabad.

e) A perusal of Ex.A2 reveals that the land was acquired at Vaddiatpally village near Nizamabad for the purpose of construction of anicut, Land Acquisition Officer has awarded @Rs.13,600/- per acre for SCW and DCW lands and the reference Court has enhanced it to Rs.20,000/- per acre.

f) Ex.A3 is the copy of judgment in O.P.No.164 of 1984 passed by the Additional District Judge, Nizamabad for the lands that were acquired for the purpose of house sites in Manikbhandar village and the reference Court has enhanced the compensation to Rs.25,000/- per acre i.e. Rs.7/- per square yard, along with other statutory benefits, while the Land Acquisition Officer has awarded Rs.17,000/- per acre.
It is elicited through the evidence of PW3 that Manikbhandar is abutting Mutyampalli village, where at the land in the present case was acquired.
g) It is elicited through the evidence of RW1 that the distance between Mutyampalli village and Vaddiatpally is only 1KM and the distance between Nizambad and Mutyampalli is about 5 KM.
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.375_2006 h)
Therefore, on an overall perusal of the evidence of PWs 1 to 3, RW1 and Exs.A1 to A3, it is held that the acquired lands in the present case are similar to those under Exs.A1 to A3.

i) The land under Ex.A2 pertains to the Vaddiatpally, which is just 1 KM away from the acquired land and it is further elicited that the land that is acquired under Ex.A3 pertains to Manikbhandar village, which is at around 1 KM and it is evident that the lands fetch more value.
The reference Court's award under Exs.A2 and A3 attained finality.

Further, the Land Acquisition Officer has not disputed with regard to the distance of these villages and it is further elicited through the evidence on record that the lands acquired are near to Nizamabad town and they were acquired for the purpose of house sites.
j) Therefore, considering the evidence on record, it is held that the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer is meager and it has to be enhanced.

It is further held that the award passed by the reference Court granting compensation @Rs.57,000/- per acre for the extent of Ac.0-25 guntas in survey Nos.696 and 699 and @ Rs.34,200/- per acre for the extent of Ac.01-17 The Land Acquisition Officer Rdo, vs G. Ashanna on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125044796/
3 guntas in survey Nos.700 and 702 of the acquired lands, is well justified.

sentences.text: Point No.1 is answered accordingly.
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.375_2006 12. POINT NO.2:
In view of the reasoned finding arrived at Point No.1, this Court holds that the judgment and decree of the reference Court do not need any interference.
13. POINT NO.3:

In the result, the appeal is dismissed upholding the judgment and decree dated 16.08.2005 passed in O.P.No.461 of 1995 by the learned I Additional District Judge,
Nizamabad.
No costs.
Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI, J ___________________________ TIRUMALA DEVI EADA, J Date: 06.03.2025 ns
